subject: Career
title: Digital Minimalism and Screen Boundaries
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Digital Minimalism and Screen Boundaries.

hook.text: He checks his phone 96 times a day. Each check fragments his attention and keeps his stress response simmering.

buildup.text: Cal Newport's Digital Minimalism: technology should serve your values. Most app usage serves the app company's values.

discovery.text: Each notification triggers a micro-stress response. Over a day, hundreds of micro-stresses compound.

twist.text: Removing social media for 30 days reduces anxiety by 25% in controlled studies. Most people feel better in days.

climax.text: Audit your phone: remove non-essential notifications, set app time limits, and designate phone-free zones.

punchline.text: Your phone is designed to steal your attention. Guard it like the resource it is.

quiz.question: What does Cal Newport's Digital Minimalism argue?
options: Technology should serve your values, not the app company's
Use as many apps as possible

details.summary: Digital minimalism is a philosophy of technology use where you focus online time on carefully selected activities that support your values and eliminate everything else. Applied to work life, it means intentionally reducing digital noise to protect cognitive capacity and recovery time.
details.whyItMatters: The average knowledge worker checks email seventy-seven times daily and touches their phone over two thousand times. Digital minimalism reclaims the attention and rest time lost to compulsive technology use.
takeaways: Intentional technology use protects attention and recovery time
Notification reduction alone measurably lowers workplace stress
A thirty-day digital declutter reveals which tools truly add value

faq.question: How is digital minimalism different from a complete digital detox?
faq.answer: A digital detox is temporary total abstinence. Digital minimalism is a permanent philosophy of intentional use. It retains technology that clearly serves your values and goals while eliminating low-value digital habits. It is sustainable because it optimizes rather than eliminates.

faq.question: What are practical first steps toward digital minimalism at work?
faq.answer: Start by disabling non-essential notifications, checking email at scheduled times rather than reactively, using website blockers during focused work, and auditing which digital tools genuinely support your most important work versus those that merely create busywork.
